loop.top3_why: The median strategy (A) delivers the lowest validation score and shows the most stable performance across the three windows, especially in the third window where it outperforms the weighted and mean options. Given the series’ strong trend and seasonality, a robust aggregation that mitigates the influence of any single model’s outlier predictions is preferable. The weighted inverse‑error approach (B) has higher variance across windows and may overfit to the limited validation set, while the plain mean (C) is consistently worse. Therefore, median is the safest choice for generalization.
loop.top3_why_not: B, while slightly better on the second window, suffers from higher error in the first and third windows and relies on inverse‑error weights that can be unstable with only three validation windows. C is consistently worse across all windows and offers no robustness advantage over A.
